mn73:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.
mn73:2.1: Then the Wanderer Vacchagotta went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
mn73:2.2: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:
mn73:3.1: “I have had conversations with Master Gotama for a long time.
mn73:3.2: It would be good if Master Gotama would show me the profitable and the unprofitable in brief.”
mn73:3.3: “I could show you the profitable and the unprofitable in brief, Vaccha, and I could show you the profitable and the unprofitable in detail;
mn73:3.4: but I will show you them in brief.
mn73:3.5: Listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”
mn73:4.1: “Greed, Vaccha, is unprofitable, non-greed is profitable;
mn73:4.2: hate is unprofitable, non-hate is profitable;
mn73:4.3: delusion is unprofitable, non-delusion is profitable.
mn73:4.4: So, Vaccha, these three things are unprofitable and three things are profitable.
mn73:5.1: Killing living beings is unprofitable, abstention from killing living beings is profitable;
mn73:5.2: taking what is not given is unprofitable, abstention from taking what is not given is profitable;
mn73:5.3: misconduct in sensual desires is unprofitable, abstention from misconduct in sensual desires is profitable;
mn73:5.4: false speech is unprofitable, abstention from false speech is profitable;
mn73:5.5: malicious speech is unprofitable, abstention from malicious speech is profitable;
mn73:5.6: harsh speech is unprofitable, abstention from harsh speech is profitable;
mn73:5.7: gossip is unprofitable, abstention from gossip is profitable;
mn73:5.8: covetousness is unprofitable, uncovetousness is profitable;
mn73:5.9: ill will is unprofitable, non-ill-will is profitable;
mn73:5.10: wrong view is unprofitable, right view is profitable.
mn73:5.11: So, Vaccha, these ten things are unprofitable and ten things are profitable.
mn73:6.1: When, Vaccha, a bhikkhu’s craving has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising, that bhikkhu is an Arahant with taints destroyed, who has lived the life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, reached his own goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and is completely liberated through final knowledge.”
mn73:7.2: Is there any one bhikkhu, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, who by realizing for himself with direct knowledge here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints?”
mn73:7.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the bhikkhus, my disciples, who by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.”
mn73:8.1: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, and let the bhikkhus’ case rest.
mn73:8.2: Is there any one bhikkhunī, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, who by realizing for herself with direct knowledge here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints?”
mn73:8.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the bhikkhunīs, my disciples, who by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.”
mn73:9.1: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, and let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest.
mn73:9.2: Is there any one lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a householder clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world?”
mn73:9.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world.”
mn73:10.1: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, and let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, rest.
mn73:10.2: Is there any one lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a householder clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out his instruction, responds to his advice, has crossed beyond doubt, is free from perplexity, has gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation?”
mn73:10.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have crossed beyond doubt, are free from perplexity, have gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation.”
mn73:11.1: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, and let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, both those living the life divine and those enjoying sensual pleasures, rest.
mn73:11.2: Is there any one female lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a housewife clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world?”
mn73:11.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the female lay followers, my disciples, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world.”
mn73:12.1: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, both those living the life divine and those enjoying sensual pleasures, rest, and let the case of the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, rest.
mn73:12.2: Is there any one female lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a housewife clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out his instruction, responds to his advice, has crossed beyond doubt, is free from perplexity, has gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation?”
mn73:12.3: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the female lay followers, my disciples, housewives clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have crossed beyond doubt, are free from perplexity, have gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation.”
mn73:13.1: “If, Master Gotama, only Master Gotama were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no bhikkhus were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.2: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.3: But since Master Gotama is accomplished in this Dhamma and the bhikkhus too are accomplished in it,
mn73:13.4: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:13.5: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no bhikkhunīs were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.6: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.7: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs are accomplished in this Dhamma,
mn73:13.8: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:13.9: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.10: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.11: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, are accomplished in this Dhamma,
mn73:13.12: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:13.13: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.14: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.15: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, are accomplished in this Dhamma,
mn73:13.16: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:13.17: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.18: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.19: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, are accomplished in this Dhamma,
mn73:13.20: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:13.21: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in it,
mn73:13.22: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
mn73:13.23: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, are accomplished in this Dhamma,
mn73:13.24: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.
mn73:14.1: Just as the river Ganges inclines towards the sea, slopes towards the sea, tends towards the sea, and merges with the sea, so too Master Gotama’s assembly, with its householders and those gone forth, inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, tends towards Nibbāna, and merges with Nibbāna.
mn73:15.1: ‘Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms. …
mn73:15.2: I go to Master Gotama for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha.
mn73:15.3: I would receive the Going-forth under Master Gotama, I would receive the Full Admission.’
mn73:16.1: “Vaccha, one who formerly belonged to another sect and wishes for the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline lives on probation for four months. At the end of the four months, bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give him the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state;
mn73:16.2: but even here I have recognized a difference between individuals.”
mn73:16.3: “Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to another sect and wish for the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months, and at the end of four months bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give them the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state, then I will live on probation for four years, and at the end of the four years let bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give me the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state.”
mn73:16.4: And Vacchagotta the Wanderer received the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, and he received the Full Admission.
mn73:17.1: Not long after his Full Admission, half a month after his Full Admission, the venerable Vacchagotta went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the venerable Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One:
mn73:17.2: “Venerable sir, I have reached whatever can be reached by the knowledge and the true knowledge of one in higher training;[^1]
mn73:17.3: let the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma further.”
mn73:18.1: “In that case, Vaccha, develop two things further: serenity and insight.
mn73:18.2: These two things, Vaccha, when developed further—serenity and insight—will lead to the penetration of the many elements.
mn73:19.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:19.2: ‘may I wield the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, may I become many; having been many, may I become one; may I appear and vanish; may I go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; may I dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; may I walk on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, may I travel through the air like a bird on the wing; with my hand may I touch and stroke the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; may I wield bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world’—
mn73:19.3: in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.
mn73:20.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:20.2: ‘may I, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, hear both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near’—in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.
mn73:21.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:21.2: ‘may I, having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with my own mind, understand them thus—
mn73:21.3: may I understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust,
mn73:21.4: and a mind without lust as a mind without lust;
mn73:21.5: may I understand a mind with hate as a mind with hate,
mn73:21.6: and a mind without hate as a mind without hate;
mn73:21.7: may I understand a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion,
mn73:21.8: and a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion;
mn73:21.9: may I understand a contracted mind as contracted,
mn73:21.10: and a distracted mind as distracted;
mn73:21.11: may I understand an exalted mind as exalted,
mn73:21.12: and an unexalted mind as unexalted;
mn73:21.13: may I understand a surpassable mind as surpassable,
mn73:21.14: and an unsurpassable mind as unsurpassable;
mn73:21.15: may I understand a concentrated mind as concentrated,
mn73:21.16: and an unconcentrated mind as unconcentrated;
mn73:21.17: may I understand a liberated mind as liberated,
mn73:21.18: and an unliberated mind as unliberated’—
mn73:21.19: in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.
mn73:22.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:22.2: ‘may I recollect my manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of world-contraction and expansion: “there I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared elsewhere; and there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared here”—thus may I recollect my manifold past lives with their aspects and particulars’—
mn73:22.3: in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.
mn73:23.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:23.2: ‘may I, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions thus: “these beings who were ill-conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of the noble ones, wrong in view, undertaking action based on wrong view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in perdition, even in hell; but these beings who were well-conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, right in view, undertaking action based on right view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a good destination, even in the heavenly world”—thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, may I see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions’—
mn73:23.3: in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.
mn73:24.1: As far as you shall wish, Vaccha:
mn73:24.2: ‘may I, by realizing for myself with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints’—
mn73:24.3: in each and every case you will attain the capacity to witness it for yourself, whenever there is an opportunity.”
mn73:25.1: Then the venerable Vacchagotta, having delighted in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on his right, he departed.
mn73:26.1: Then the venerable Vacchagotta, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, before long entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the life divine, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge here and now.
mn73:26.2: He directly knew: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’
mn73:26.3: And the venerable Vacchagotta became one of the Arahants.
mn73:27.1: Now on that occasion a number of bhikkhus were going to see the Blessed One.
mn73:27.2: The venerable Vacchagotta saw those bhikkhus coming in the distance.
mn73:27.3: Seeing them, he went up to them and said to them:
mn73:27.4: “Now then, where are you venerable ones going?”
mn73:27.5: “We are going to see the Blessed One, friend.”
mn73:27.6: “Then, venerable ones, please pay homage with your heads at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, and say thus:
mn73:27.7: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and he says:
mn73:27.8: “the Blessed One has been served by me, the Fortunate One has been served by me.”’”[^2]
mn73:28.1: “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Vacchagotta.
mn73:28.2: Then those bhikkhus went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side. When they had done so, they said to the Blessed One:
mn73:28.3: “Venerable sir, the venerable Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and he says:
mn73:28.4: ‘the Blessed One has been served by me, the Fortunate One has been served by me.’”
mn73:28.5: “Bhikkhus, I already knew the bhikkhu Vacchagotta by encompassing his mind with my own mind, thus:
mn73:28.6: ‘the bhikkhu Vacchagotta has the three true knowledges; he has great supernormal power and great might.’
mn73:28.7: And deities also told me of this matter:
mn73:28.8: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta has the three true knowledges; he has great supernormal power and great might.’”
mn73:28.9: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn73:28.10: Those bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
